findings.reason: Confirmed. Items /24–/27, /30 and /31 are missing and sit in route 1 (NC.5). /24's note says 'No p-adic height exists … in any atlas layer … NC.5 needs it'. PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24's route 2 (part-ii; parent SelmerIwasawaCohomology, roadmap SelmerComplexesAndPadicHeights, area iwasawa) plans the general theory. Its brief covers 'Nekovář's p-adic height pairing' and 'the height pairing on H^1_f and on cycles (A.5) with its decomposition into local terms'. It tests 'for X a curve (n = 2) and divisors of degree 0, recover Nekovář's height pairing on Selmer groups of the Jacobian'. Its review accepted it ('This is where Appendix A belongs'). NC.5 plans only 'the depth-two quotient and p-adic height equations, Néron–Severi contributions and all bad-place local terms'. Each record assumes the other owns the general pairing: the Part II's brief says 'the atlas has p-adic heights only for curves (… NC.5 …)'. So the duplication is real, and §15 puts the general pairing in the Part II. Three corrections to the claim. (a) The Part II was proposed on 22 September (#1957), the day before this extraction (#2202); only its acceptance (#2572, 24 September) came later. (b) PAPER-DISEGNI-22's reuse of the route was rejected by its review ('No second foundational implementation is approved'). (c) 'Its brief plans exactly this' overstates. The brief plans the pairing 'under (V1)–(V3)', and (V3) is the Panchishkin condition at p (PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24/51), which yields a canonical splitting of the Hodge filtration. /24, like p.901, fixes an arbitrary splitting s and assumes no ordinarity. Adjusted fix. The items cannot be made planned: under §16 an item is planned only when a layer plans it, and the Part II has no layers yet (its design, DESIGN-SelmerIwasawaCohomologyPartII, issue #3430, is pending). Instead, move /24, /25, /26, /27, /30 and /31 from route 1 to a part-ii route with DISEGNI-LIU-24 route 2's exact parent, roadmap id, title and area, so that the queue adds it to that design. /25 and /30 must move too. /26 and /27 are stated on /25's categories and on (π_1, π_2), and /31 on /30's E_1 and E_2; left in NC.5, they would make the Part II depend on items owned downstream of it. The route's brief asks for the pairing with a general splitting under Nekovář's conditions [Nek93, §2.1.2], with the curve case V = H^1_ét(X_Q̄,Q_p)* [Nek93, §5.3] and this paper's §§3.1–3.3 as its test. It names NC.5 as a consumer and says the Part II must not import NC.5. On the assembled atlas, none of the Part II's imports is downstream of an AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty stage, so NC.5 can import it without a cycle. /28, /32, /33 and /35–/38 stay in route 1. Update /24's note, the route-1 reason, the summary and the report. If the design has been merged by the time of the fix, route the items to its layers instead.

Confirmed. /1 is planned at Tau Ceti ModularCurves layers 9 and 10, with the note that 'X_s(ℓ) and X_ns(ℓ) are instances'. But layer 10 fixes its class 'once' as 'the diamond-operator quotients of [Γ₁(N)] and nothing else: for N ≥ 5 prime', and 'not arbitrary finite quotients of Layer 9, for which none of the assertions below is made'. Layer 9 plans affine quotients (9A, 9D). Its regularity results cover the semi-Borel subgroups and product subgroups of the diagonal Cartan, not Cartan normalisers. So the compactified X_s(ℓ) and X_ns(ℓ), their cusps and the moduli meaning of their rational points are unplanned. No stage and no declaration at Tau Ceti f790474 has a Cartan-level curve. The accepted review of PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23 reads these layers the same way: 'layer 10 compactifies only diamond quotients, and ModularCurvesPartII R13.4a only full, Γ₁ and Γ₀ level. Stays missing.' /71 is an isomorphism of generic fibres, while R13.5 computes 'the local models and supersingular intersections', so R13.5 is the wrong owner. The quotations on pp.887, 888 and 926 match. Conjugation by diag(ℓ,1) carries Γ₀(ℓ²) to matrices that are diagonal mod ℓ and w_{ℓ²} to an antidiagonal matrix, which gives /71. Corrections: 9D does plan the affine coarse Y_H; X_0(ℓ²) is already at R13.4a, which treats 'refined Γ₀ level' at general n through R13.2; and layer 10 is no input to /1 at all. Adjusted fix: route /1 and /71 by a source route to ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a. The layer gains, in general form, the compactified X_H over Z[1/ℓ] for H ≤ GL₂(F_ℓ) with −I ∈ H and surjective determinant (instances C_s(ℓ)^+ and C_ns(ℓ)^+). It also gains w_{ℓ²} on X_0(ℓ²), the quotient X_0^+(ℓ²), /71, and the rational-point criterion for j ∉ {0, 1728}. No twist is needed there, since −I ∈ H, and 0 and 1728 are CM j-invariants. R13.4a 'does not use analytic uniformization', and R14.1 is downstream of it, so w_{ℓ²} and /71 are stated through the moduli interpretation there. The paper's 'conjugation with (ℓ 0; 0 1)' is the upper-half-plane form, which belongs downstream at R13.4b. On the assembled atlas, ED.6, NC.5 and NC.2 can import R13.4a without a cycle, and R13.5, which keeps /72–/76, is downstream of it. For the maintainer: the Part II EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic (PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23 route 2, accepted, design pending) plans Cartan-level X(H) because R13.4a lacked them; once R13.4a has X_H, that design should import it. The new item of /7 consumes the reworked /1 and /71, so this fixer is best placed to add it.

Confirmed. /58 is planned at ColemanIntegration:L1, and its statement ends with Besser's theorem: with Coleman integrals, the same formula is 'the unique unipotent Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism A_n^dR(b_0,x_0) → A_n^dR(b,x) for any b, b_0, x, x_0'. L1 builds Coleman integration directly, 'so that no general Tannakian theorem is an unowned prerequisite'. No stage and no packet node plans a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of path torsors, and the packet explicitly sets aside Besser's Tannakian argument. L1/word-algebra calls U 'a unipotent connection' and states Chen's composition of paths, but that is not such an isomorphism. So /58's note and the report's 'Besser's Tannakian iterated integrals' at L1 are wrong. The p.921 quotation matches. arXiv v1 §5.1 states the theorem for path torsors: π_1^dR(Y_Qp; z_1, z_2) 'contains a unique Frobenius invariant element' [Bes02, 3.2]. Two corrections. (a) The §5.3.2 splitting does not need the theorem. There b_0 and x_0 are the Teichmüller representatives of b and x (p.920), so τ_{b,x} stays inside residue disks, and α_φ = ∫ω uses only Frobenius-equivariance of abelian Coleman integration, which L1 plans. The theorem is used in Lemma 5.7, whose (49) (p.925) moves the base point to another residue disk, and so in §6.6. (b) Part (a) of the fix over-claims. Only (40), the formal iterated integrals on one residue disk, is L1 material (L1/word-algebra-local-expansion). (41) describes τ_{b,x} on the path torsor through the trivialisation (39) and rests on /42 (Lemma 4.3) and /56 (Theorem 5.3), both missing on route 2. Adjusted fix: (40) planned at L1; (41) and Besser's theorem missing, on route 2 (NC.2). The new item cites L1/word-algebra-frobenius and L1/coleman-realization as its analytic input, so that NC.2 builds only the bridge to the Tannakian path torsors. On the assembled atlas, L1 feeds NC.2 directly and NC.2 does not reach L1, so there is no cycle. NC.4, whose unipotent Albanese map needs the same bridge, is downstream of NC.2.

Confirmed. /79 is planned at HE.7 and GZ.8 and states 'If ord_{s=1} L(f,s) = 1, then rk A_f(Q) = dim A_f [GZ86, KL89]'. The accepted PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/304 is missing, with the note 'no stage states the rank ≥ m / BSD-up-to-ℚ^× conclusion for A_f over ℚ', and is routed to GZ.8. GZ.8 specialises to 'X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient, …' and states no rank bound for A_f. HE.7 plans the Kolyvagin–Logachev extension in conditional form: a non-torsion Heegner point gives the rank and finite Sha. Two records the red team did not cite support the finding. RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.3 plans the assembly (K from BSD.2, GZ.8's non-torsion Heegner point, then HE.7) for elliptic curves only. PAPER-SKINNER-20/2 records the A_f theorem as planned, and its review note says that 'no stage assembles the A_f theorem'. The p.927 quotation matches. Corrections: /304 is broader than the lower bound, since it includes the m-or-≥3m dichotomy and BSD up to ℚ^×. And HE.7 plans the upper bound only in conditional form: deriving it from ord = 1 needs the same missing assembly. Adjusted fix: (a) missing: 'if each L(f^σ,s) has a simple zero at s = 1, then rk A_f(Q) ≥ dim A_f', routed to GZ.8 beside GZ-86/304, with a note naming BSD.3's steps and saying that BSD.3 is for elliptic curves. (b) Planned at HE.7 in HE.7's form: a non-torsion Heegner point y_K ∈ A_f(K) gives rank A_f(K) = dim A_f and finite Ш(A_f/K), so rk A_f(Q) ≤ dim A_f. /82 uses (a) and (b) together. For the maintainer: whether GZ.8 or a RankZeroOneBSD stage owns the A_f assembly, which SKINNER-20/2 needs too.

Confirmed. The quotations on pp.924, 930–931, 931 and 933 match. p.894 (§1.7) adds that the method's differential equations are solved 'using algorithms of the fourth author [Tui16], [Tui17]'. The algorithm gives Fr_q at q = 3, 7 and 11 and the lifts on ]U_1[ and ]U_2[. /60 states (45) but no algorithm, /84 takes A_q as given, and /87 cites [Tui16] only for the lift. No stage text names Tuitman's or Kedlaya's algorithm, and 'Tuitman' occurs in no other extraction. Correction to the evidence: the rigid-cohomology packet already plans the hyperelliptic case, RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification (Kedlaya's lift, the reduction and integral reconstruction). Frobenius lifts are at RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra, and H^1 of the dagger algebra at RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves. Tuitman's algorithm generalises the Kedlaya node to curves with a map to P¹. Adjustments. (a) Owner: under §15, route the new item by a source route to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7, beside the Kedlaya node, rather than to ED.6. ED.6 consumes it, and so could ED.4, whose Coleman integrals need the same Frobenius matrices. The new edge closes no cycle: on the assembled atlas ED.6 has no outgoing edge, and neither RD.4 nor RD.7 reaches ED.4 or ED.6. (b) Take the hypotheses from [Tui16] and [Tui17]: good reduction at p, and their conditions on the plane model monic in y and on x: X → P¹. Remark 6.1 is not one of them: it explains the choice p = 17, and the paper runs the algorithm at q = 3 and 7, where by that remark the basis is not integral. (c) The [BT17]/[AS05] part is already done: /92's statement cites [BT17, Props. 3.8, 4.3] and /82's note cites [AS05]. Adding Agashe–Stein to the prerequisites is optional (Math. Comp. 74 (2005), 10.1090/S0025-5718-04-01644-8, per Crossref).

Confirmed. Definition A.2 (p.935) asks only that a morphism (E,e) → (V,v) exist, and the next paragraph says that a universal object 'is unique up to unique isomorphism'. arXiv v1 (p.34) has the same wording, and item /68 copies both. The counterexample holds under the paper's own conventions. Take E' = A_n ⊕ 1 with e' = (1,0), E'_0 = E' and E'_i = I^iA_n for i ≥ 1. The graded pieces are 1 ⊕ 1 and I^iA_n/I^{i+1}A_n, so (E',e') is pointed n-unipotent. Compose the projection to (A_n,1) with a ↦ av. The second map sends I^iA_n into I^iV ⊂ V_i, because I kills each V_i/V_{i+1}. So every (V,v) receives a morphism that respects the filtrations, while dim ω(E') = dim A_n + 1. The intended definition includes uniqueness. Theorem 4.2 (p.910) says that (A_n^dR(Y),1) is universal 'in the sense of Section A.1. That is, … there exists a unique map'. The proof of Lemma 5.2 (p.919) says that a morphism of universal objects 'is determined by where it sends 1'. The proof of Lemma A.4 (p.936) needs uniqueness for Hom(ω_n,ν_n) → ν(A_n(C,ω)) to be onto: existence gives only injectivity. So this is a misprint that affects nothing, as the red team says. E9 is new. E6 concerns Theorem 4.2's 'section of V', a different slip. Medium fits: /68 is false as written, but the correction is one word and changes no other item. The fix stands as proposed.

Confirmed. /6 states Theorem 1.2, but its note accounts only for ℓ ≥ 11. The paper's only justification is 'Together with the results of Bilu–Parent and Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo, this allows us to complete the characterisation' (p.888), and those results concern ℓ > 7 (p.887). arXiv v1 states the existence half outright: '… if and only if ℓ ≤ 7'. /75 covers only ℓ ≡ 1 mod 12. The argument holds. X_0(4), X_0(9) and X_0(25) have genus 0. X_0(49) has genus 1, but w_49 has h(−196) = 4 fixed points, so X_0^+(49) has genus 0 by Riemann–Hurwitz (equivalently, 49a has root number +1). The cusps 0 and ∞ are rational and swapped by w_{ℓ²}, so X_s(ℓ) ≅ P¹_Q for ℓ ≤ 7. Only finitely many rational points are cusps or CM. Correction: no twist is needed. Since −I ∈ C_s(ℓ)^+, for j ∉ {0, 1728} every E/Q with that j-invariant has image in a conjugate of C_s(ℓ)^+. Low sits at the medium boundary, since this is a missing proof input rather than presentation, but the effect is small: /6 is stated correctly and is already missing and routed. Adjusted fix: add a separate theorem item, routed with /6 to ED.6. Its inputs are the reworked /1 and /71 at R13.4a (finding /2), the genera above and the rational cusp. The fixer of /2 is best placed to add it.

Confirmed. All three are in the published text, and none affects a result. (1) Definition A.1 (p.934) reads 'every object V ∈ C admits a nonzero morphism 1 −→ V'. The zero object admits none, so as printed no Tannakian category is unipotent. 'Every nonzero object' is the standard criterion: an affine group scheme over a field is unipotent exactly when every nonzero representation has a nonzero fixed vector. arXiv v1 (p.34) has the same sentence, so E10's locator names both versions. /67 copies it. (2) The [Nek93] entry (p.943) ends 'https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-005-0696-y'. Crossref, queried today, gives that DOI as van der Laan, Talman and Yang, 'Solving discrete zero point problems', Mathematical Programming (2006). It gives 10.1007/978-1-4757-4271-8_8 as Nekovář, 'On p-adic height pairings', Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris, 1990–91. p.940 prints '[BL04] … Complex Abelian Barieties'. arXiv v1 gives [Nek93] with no DOI (p.40) and [BL04] as 'Complex abelian varieties' (p.39), so E11 is published-only, as the red team says. The extraction's prerequisites use the right DOI, and neither its report nor its result mentions the printed one. (3) Corollary 6.7 (p.929) claims good reduction outside 13. Its proof, 'The result follows from Theorem 6.6. Indeed, we may contract all three rational curves', covers only the 13-adic part, since Theorem 6.6 concerns X_s(ℓ) over Q_ℓ^nr(ϖ). The paper supports the claim elsewhere: p.930 says Baran's first model 'has good reduction away from 13'. The review checked this ('the first model is singular only modulo 13'). The remark about 2 is right: the proof of Theorem 6.6 uses that 'the order of w_{ℓ²} is invertible on O_X', which holds at ℓ but not at 2. 'Affects nothing' for E12 matches the file's other gaps, E4 and E8. Adjustments: E10's locator names Definition A.1 at p.934 and arXiv v1 p.34, and /76's note should cite the p.930 model as the paper's own route. The fixes stand otherwise.
